questions.question: A global laptop manufacturer has manufacturing facilities in China and Vietnam, while its largest markets are Europe and North America. The company recently experienced: • Pandemic-related factory shutdowns • Tariff increases • Political conflicts affecting trade • Shipping delays extending delivery times by 40 days • Customer complaints due to delayed product launches The CEO wants to know whether production should remain in Asia or be relocated closer to major markets. As a Global Procurement Consultant, prepare a detailed report addressing: a) Explain why globalization alone is no longer sufficient for modern procurement strategies. (3 Marks) b) Compare offshoring, nearshoring, and reshoring using suitable examples. (5 Marks) c) Analyze how reshoring and nearshoring improve supply chain resilience, procurement efficiency, and customer satisfaction. (5 Marks) d) Discuss the potential challenges and risks involved in implementing these strategies. (3 Marks) e) Recommend the best sourcing strategy for the company with suitable justification and expected long-term outcomes. (4 Marks)

questions.question: A large retail company sources garments from suppliers in different countries. The company recently discovered that one of its major suppliers has been accused of paying low wages, providing unsafe working conditions and employing workers for excessive hours. There are also concerns that the supplier maintains incomplete records and has failed to comply with certain labour and environmental requirements. The company’s procurement manager, however, is reluctant to discontinue the supplier because it offers lower prices and ensures timely delivery. Some employees have also raised concerns that supplier selection may not always be transparent. As a Procurement Manager, answer the following: a) Identify the major ethical issues involved in the above situation. (5 marks) b) Explain how the company can fulfil its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) towards workers and other stakeholders in its supply chain. (5 marks) c) Explain the important components of a supply chain governance framework that can help prevent such issues. (5 marks) d) Suggest measures that the company should adopt to ensure ethical and responsible global sourcing. (5 marks)

questions.question: Godrej Consumer Products conducted a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) to assess the environmental impact of a soap bar throughout its entire life cycle, from raw material sourcing to packaging disposal. The study covered four stages: raw materials, manufacturing, packaging and transportation, and use and disposal. The LCA showed that the raw material stage, particularly palm oil cultivation, contributed significantly to the product’s environmental impact due to land and water use. This highlighted impacts that were not apparent when the company focused mainly on factory operations. Based on the findings, the company began working with certified sustainable palm oil suppliers and reduced plastic in some packaging. Questions: a) Define Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on the case. b) Explain the four stages examined in the LCA of the soap bar. c) Analyse why the raw material stage had a significant environmental impact. d) Evaluate how the LCA findings influenced Godrej’s procurement and packaging decisions.
questions.solution_html: Detailed essay covering conceptual foundations, mathematical formulation, and critical analysis. (10 Marks)
